about:
Tampa Sheet Metal Company was founded in 1920 by John Jiretz Sr., a craftsman who learned his trade in Austria and Germany. The company is located in Tampa, Florida, and remains family-owned, currently managed by John L. Jiretz (president, grandson of the founder) and John D. Jiretz (great-grandson). It began as a sheet metal fabrication business using hand tools and has evolved into a modern facility.

The company provides full-service sheet metal fabrication from design to finished product. Processes include laser cutting (4,000-watt laser cutting stainless steel, steel, aluminum, brass, copper on a 60x120-inch table), CNC turret punching (36-station, 45-ton press), press braking (12-foot and 6-foot capacity), metal shearing (12-foot, quarter-inch thick steel), robotic welding (steel, aluminum, stainless steel), hardware insertion, countersinking, counterboring, and mechanical assembly. The facility spans 25,000 square feet near downtown Tampa.

Tampa Sheet Metal serves industrial, commercial, and construction sectors. Project examples from the company's archive include industrial facilities, shopping malls, high-rise buildings, EPC projects, infrastructure, and commercial buildings.

The company emphasizes its long-standing dedication to quality and service since 1920, with a quality control program certified by FM Approvals and Keystone Certifications. It also highlights environmental responsibility, noting that sheet metal is 100% recyclable and all scrap is melted down for reuse.
